stories.title: A hybrid deep learning framework for robust and efficient streamflow prediction under varying data availability
stories.description: Accurate daily runoff prediction is essential for water resource management and flood control. However, intensifying climate change has amplified the nonlinearity and non-stationarity of runoff series, creating a critical trilemma for deep learning methods: the inability to simultaneously achieve local and long-range feature modeling, computational efficiency, and physical interpretability. To address this challenge, we propose a novel deep learning architecture—the Deep Temporal Gated Residual Network (DTGR)—that synergistically integrates three neural network modules: (i) the Deep Convolutional Residual Module (DCRM), which employs multi-scale causal convolutions to extract hierarchical local temporal features; (ii) the Temporal Encoding Module (TEM), which utilizes linear multi-head attention to model long-range dependencies with O(n) computational complexity; and (iii) the Gate Decoding Module (GDM), which implements adaptive gating mechanisms to dynamically fuse local and global representations. The model was validated across four hydrologically distinct basins—rainfall-driven, snowmelt-dominated, and mixed regimes—achieving Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency coefficients of 0.826–0.951 for univariate prediction, outperforming seven benchmarks by 6.7%–39.7% in overall accuracy, with NRMSE reductions of 15.7%–57.3%. Under multivariate inputs, NRMSE further drops 20.9%–55.2%, with cross-site NSE variation as low as 0.014. Computationally, DTGR cuts training time by 47% and memory usage by 38%–44% versus Transformers. Mechanistically, SHAP interpretability analysis confirms that DTGR’s learned feature importance aligns with basin-specific physical processes—temperature-driven snowmelt dynamics and precipitation-runoff responses—validating that the architecture achieves interpretability without sacrificing predictive accuracy. These results demonstrate that modular co-design of neural network components can resolve fundamental trade-offs in hydrological deep learning, delivering an o delivering a computationally efficient solution for real-time flood forecasting.
